# `factory_test_control`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Run one factory-test operation (park, delete user data, set language, enter shipping mode).

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / probable (64-bit build; 32-bit build probable) |
| Side-effect tier | C |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, handler @0xe1490, Execute @0x142b80 (64-bit build) |

Every successfully parsed request replies with integer result 0 and code 0, even when the operation itself fails; operation outcome, pending status and failures are reported in a FactoryTestControl event (members Event, Timestamp, operation, state complete or fail, optional error and code, optional record, optional pending). Parse failures return an error reply with no result. The event is broadcast before the RPC reply unless the event object contains the exact raw text "pending":true (a raw substring search, not a parsed check), in which case the completion event comes later from a deferred worker. The record member is normally an array of metadata record objects but a single object for enterShippingMode; each record may carry userId, timestamp, platform, appVersion and osVersion. Destructive: do not send to a device you are not prepared to wipe or shut down.

Side effects: scopePark homes the mount. delUserImages deletes the stored user images and saves a record. delLicense remounts read-write and deletes licence files. setLangEn sets the language to English and forwards the setting to the secondary unit on that branch. enterShippingMode performs a privileged hardware register write, clears shipping records and on success schedules a shutdown. Synchronous operations can block on shell and record I/O; no upper bound on elapsed time is established.

## Request params

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | any | yes | - | Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"factory_test_control"`. [READ] |
| `params` | object | yes | - | Required object (107 if absent, null, scalar or array). No other keys are passed on. [READ] |
| `params.operation` | string | yes | - | Operation to run, matched case-sensitively. scopePark homes the mount (completion may be deferred), delUserImages deletes user images asynchronously, delLicense deletes licence files, setLangEn sets the language to English, enterShippingMode clears shipping records and, on success, schedules a shutdown. Any other string, including the empty string, is accepted by the RPC (result 0) and reported as a failure through the FactoryTestControl event. One of: `scopePark`, `delUserImages`, `delLicense`, `setLangEn`, `enterShippingMode`. [READ] |
| `params.userId` | string | no | - | Optional metadata string stored in the record. Default empty (omitted from the record when empty). Wrong type is rejected with 105. [READ] |
| `params.timestamp` | integer | no | 0 | Optional metadata integer. The low 32 bits are stored with no range check and the record omits it when the signed value is 0 or negative. The app sends epoch milliseconds, which can lose high bits (INFERRED); the firmware intended unit is unresolved. Wrong type, including explicit null, is rejected with 104. [READ] |
| `params.platform` | string | no | - | Optional metadata string (the app sends Android). Default empty. Wrong type is rejected with 105. [READ] |
| `params.appVersion` | string | no | - | Optional metadata string. Default empty. Wrong type is rejected with 105. [READ] |
| `params.osVersion` | string | no | - | Optional metadata string. Default empty. Wrong type is rejected with 105. [READ] |

## Reply

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `jsonrpc` | string | no | - | (both) Added by the socket layer (reply object constructor), not the handler fragment. Normally present; absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply. Receivers MUST NOT require it. Fixed value `"2.0"`. [READ; also OBSERVED on the wire (2026-10-12)] |
| `Timestamp` | string | no | - | (both) Decimal string `<seconds>.<nanoseconds>` with exactly nine fractional digits, formatted with `%ld.%09ld` from clock_gettime clock id 1. Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). On replies it is added by the socket layer and is normally present; receivers MUST NOT require it on replies (absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply). On events it is always written by the event constructor. [READ; wire shape also OBSERVED (2026-10-12)] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | (success) The request method, echoed. [READ] |
| `result` | integer | yes | - | (success) For these methods the result is the integer 0. Fixed value `0`. [READ] |
| `code` | integer | yes | - | (success) Fixed value `0`. [READ] |
| `id` | any | yes | - | (success) Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | if the request had an id and a string method (handler errors and 103), except a locally built stop_func relay failure | - | (error) The request method, echoed. Absent on dispatcher errors 100 and 200 and on a stop_func relay failure. [READ] |
| `error` | string | yes | - | (error) Message looked up from the code; unknown codes yield "fail to operate". [READ] |
| `code` | integer | yes | - | (error) Nonzero. A requested code of 0 is coerced to 207. [READ] |
| `id` | any | yes | - | (error) The request id echoed with its JSON type; null on dispatcher errors 100 and 200, where it is the only way to recognise the reply and cannot be matched to a request. [READ] |

## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 107 | Params not an object | `expected object param` |
| 105 | operation missing or not a string, or a string metadata member of the wrong type | `expected string param` |
| 104 | timestamp present and not an integer | `expected int param` |
| 200 | Dispatcher: request has no id | `invalid id` |
| 100 | Dispatcher: method missing or not a string | `invalid request` |

Operation failures (including unsupported operation strings, helper code 102) are reported only through the FactoryTestControl event, not as RPC error replies.

## Example

Request, set-language:

```json
{"id":51,"method":"factory_test_control","params":{"operation":"setLangEn"}}
```

Request, with-metadata:

```json
{"id":52,"method":"factory_test_control","params":{"operation":"scopePark","userId":"example-user","timestamp":1700000000,"platform":"Android","appVersion":"1.0.0","osVersion":"14"}}
```

Reply, ok:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"factory_test_control","result":0,"code":0,"id":51}
```

Reply, error:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"factory_test_control","error":"expected object param","code":107,"id":53}
```
